problem: The platform currently has no account-scoped default workspace, so first-time users must create and choose a workspace before they can enter their business context.
invariants: Each account has at most one default workspace.
An account's default workspace is active and accessible to that account.
Default provisioning is idempotent under repeated and concurrent requests.
Workspace reads and writes remain scoped to the trusted authenticated subject.
Default provisioning does not create or modify Identity projects or memberships.

context.outcome: Every authenticated platform account has an account-scoped default workspace named My workspace, created on first dashboard access when none exists.
context.scope: default workspace is per Identity account; the workspace remains a normal PlatformWorkspace aggregate

policies: Identity authenticates the account; PlatformWorkspace owns default selection and membership authorization.

The first default provisioning reuses the earliest active workspace owned by the account when present, renames it My workspace, and records it as default; otherwise it creates one.

acceptanceCriteria: An account with no accessible owned workspace gets one active workspace named My workspace on first authenticated dashboard load.
Repeated default provisioning returns the same default workspace without duplicates.
An account's existing earliest active owned workspace is renamed My workspace and recorded as its default on first provisioning.
Two accounts can each have a My workspace with globally unique slugs.
A member cannot have a workspace set as default unless that membership is active.
The workspace list indicates which item is the authenticated account's default.
The API and BFF do not accept the acting account identifier from browser input.

assumptions.statement: Default workspace provisioning is lazy on first authenticated dashboard access because the Identity registration lifecycle does not currently own PlatformWorkspace provisioning.
When an account already owns workspaces but has no default pointer, the earliest active owned workspace becomes the default and its name is normalized to My workspace.

decisions: Keep the default designation on an account-to-workspace pointer so a shared workspace can be a default for more than one member if needed.
Use an idempotent command rather than adding creation side effects to the workspace-list query.
